cases.prompt: I need to set up a typed API layer for my React app so we stop calling fetch everywhere. How should it look?
expectations: Creates exactly one apiClient in shared/api-client/ (client.ts, error.ts, types.ts, config.ts) as the only fetch boundary.
Makes every verb return the unwrapped data payload typed by the caller and throw an ApiError on failure.
Keeps the client framework-free — no toasts, router, or React inside it.
Adds a lint rule (no-restricted-imports/no-restricted-globals) banning fetch/axios outside shared/api-client/.

cases.prompt: The backend sometimes renames fields and I get undefined deep in my components. How do I stop that?
expectations: Runs a schema parse at the boundary (e.g. Zod invoiceSchema.parse(raw)) that converts unknown wire JSON into a typed domain value.
Explains parse-don't-validate: the parsed value is trusted downstream, so components write no defensive ?. chains.
Surfaces contract drift at the edge with a typed failure instead of leaking undefined three components deep.
Notes a 2xx with an unparseable body is a contract violation that throws INVALID_RESPONSE, not a silent undefined.

cases.prompt: In my InvoiceList component I just do const res = await fetch('/api/invoices') and use res. Is that a problem?
expectations: Flags the raw fetch as a boundary bypass: no fetch/axios/XMLHttpRequest outside shared/api-client/.
Routes the call through the typed client, e.g. await apiClient.get<Invoice[]>(`/invoices`).
Wraps it in a typed query/mutation hook rather than calling the client from a component.
Mentions the missing envelope unwrap and unhandled typed errors as additional problems.

cases.prompt: My loadInvoice function keeps getting called with a customer id. Can I make the compiler catch that?
expectations: Brands domain IDs as nominal types (InvoiceId, CustomerId) using a Brand<T, B> helper with a unique symbol.
Shows that loadInvoice(customerId) is a compile error while loadInvoice(invoiceId) passes.
Brands IDs at the parse boundary so every ID in the app is already nominal.
Notes the runtime cost is zero because brands erase at compile time.

cases.prompt: The server returns validation errors per field but I keep throwing new Error(string). How should I handle write failures and show them on the form?
expectations: Collapses every failure mode (server error envelope, non-2xx, malformed body, network, abort) into one ApiError with a machine code, status, and optional fields.
Never throws a bare new Error(string) from the data layer.
Maps server per-field errors onto form fields using error.hasFieldErrors and error.fields (form.setError per field).
Never shows error.message directly to users; resolves error.messageKey through i18n instead.

cases.prompt: Some endpoints return { data: ... } and 204s return nothing. How do I keep response handling consistent?
expectations: Uses one envelope: { data } on success or { error } on failure, unwrapped once in the client.
Handles 204 No Content as undefined, { error } as a throw, and { data } as the returned payload.
Synthesizes an ApiError for a non-2xx response with no well-formed envelope.
Ensures callers only ever see a typed payload or a typed throw, never the raw envelope.
